title: Count Binary Palindromic Numbers
summary: Given a non-negative integer n, count how many integers k between 0 and n inclusive have a binary representation that is a palindrome.
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, count how many integers k between 0 and n inclusive have a binary representation that is a palindrome.
constraints: Binary representations have no leading zeros; zero is represented by 0.
Count palindromic representations in the inclusive range.
hints: A length-L binary palindrome is determined by its first ceil(L/2) bits, whose leading bit is one.
Count all shorter lengths, then compare the palindrome mirrored from n’s own leading half.
Add 2^(ceil(L/2)-1) per shorter length, count smaller current-length prefixes, and conditionally include the mirrored candidate.
Prefixes order their mirrored palindromes monotonically, so the prefix count plus one comparison gives the exact inclusive rank.
editorial: Prefixes order their mirrored palindromes monotonically, so the prefix count plus one comparison gives the exact inclusive rank.

tests.explanation: Zero, one, three, five, seven, and nine are the six palindromes.
Zero itself is included and considered palindromic.
